text: Both legacy criteria of RWB-E4-044 are kept word for word and are exercised on a synthetic proceeds set of this run: case RC-2026-000611 of account A-0611, one receipt of source AUCTION on business date 2026-11-22 with amount 820,000.00 THB, matched to case RC-2026-000611 with matched_to SALE_PROCEEDS, and one receipt with no case reference that stays UNMATCHED. The proceeds detail behind the generic legacy lines is filled from FSD P8 A2.4 and TSD P8 T3.1, and the four legacy test case IDs keep their own rows in the Test Cases master.
why: The legacy criteria and their four test cases name no case, receipt, source, amount or date, the FSD main success criterion is one line marked 'Written one epic ahead', and the split plan gives the slice no requirement id, so the story cannot be built or tested without a stated set.
read: Legacy RWB-E4-044 (Story, Acceptance criteria, Data, Test cases); FSD P8 v3 A2.4.4.1; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; work package line for RWB-P8-E4044-APP

text: The two consumed reads are carried as placeholders and built against their fakes: the case reference is read on rwb-case and the proceeds arm of the rule package on rwb-decision, each with a one-hop, 2 s contract and a breaker, and MatchRequest carries the case, the account, the amount, the received date and the matched-to value and no other element. The payment facts themselves are read on the service's own view recovery.v_ace_payment, so no source-data operation is consumed by this slice.
why: No source publishes the operation names of the two consumed reads and TSD P8 does not enumerate the MatchRequest elements, so the contract and the fakes have to be stated from the documents.

confirm: P3 case owner and P7 rule owner at the contract tag review
impact: The consumed rows, the fakes and the request element list only; the two provided operations, the base and the rights are unchanged

text: The proceeds arm runs inside the JOB-07 run and evaluates the match package of rwb-decision at the version in force; the amount tolerance, the window before and after, the grace days, the priority and the partial floor are rule rows read at run time and never values of the build; the service holds no copy of payment_match_rule; and the rule ID and the package version are recorded with every answer before the row is written.
why: No source publishes the package code, the rule IDs or any threshold of the proceeds arm, the ownership map gives P8 only the proceeds table, and the action cannot be evaluated, asserted or reviewed without a stated reading.
read: FSD P8 v3 A2.4.3.1; TSD P8 v2 T3.1 and T3.2; context pack P8 tables; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 R-LIT-65 and R-LIT-72
confirm: P7 rule owner and the P8 solution architect at the rule package review

text: The run is one event-started Temporal workflow per business date on queue rwb-payment in namespace rwb-recovery, started by the ACE batch completion of source ALS read on recovery.v_ace_batch_status (AceDataReady, EV-26), with one matching activity that writes the decision record, the proceeds row and the outbox row in one transaction; there is no Temporal Schedule and no Quartz row, and the workflow and activity names are set at build and carried as placeholders until then.
why: The context pack lists the two jobs and zero workflows, no source names the workflow or the activity, and no source states the trigger form of the run, so the baseline has to fix one reading to be testable.

text: proceeds.account_payment_id carries the ACE payment code of recovery.v_ace_payment and nothing else; the payment itself is resolved on that view, the service holds no account or payment copy, and no account_payment table is declared in rwb_payment.
why: TSD P8 declares the cross reference and an account_payment relationship, but no owner of the ownership map declares such an object and the FSD reads the payment facts from the ACE view.
